title: System Prompts and Custom Instructions
description: Learn how persistent context shapes AI behavior — and how to set up custom instructions that make every interaction more relevant to you.

data.text: Most users type the same context in every chat: "I am a [role]", "I prefer [style]", "I work in [field]". System prompts and custom instructions let you set this context once and have it apply automatically to every conversation — making AI more useful from the very first message.

A system prompt is a set of instructions placed before the conversation begins. The AI reads it first, and it conditions every response that follows. In consumer apps like ChatGPT it is called "Custom Instructions". In developer contexts it is the "system" role in the API.

data.caption: The system prompt is always present at the start of every conversation — it shapes all AI responses before you type a single word
data.definition:
graph TD
  SP["🔧 System Prompt\n(always present)\nRole + rules + context\nfor this AI instance"] --> CTX
  USER["👤 Your message"] --> CTX
  CTX["Conversation context\n(system prompt + your messages\n+ previous replies)"] --> LLM
  LLM["Language Model"] --> RESP["AI Response\n(shaped by system prompt\n+ conversation)"]

  style SP fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#9a6700
  style LLM fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da
  style RESP fill:#d1f3d8,stroke:#1a7f37

data.text: ChatGPT's Custom Instructions feature (Settings → Personalization → Custom Instructions) lets you set two persistent blocks: (1) About you — context about your role and background; (2) How you want ChatGPT to respond — tone, format preferences, what to avoid.

data.title: Example: Custom Instructions for a product manager
data.content:
About me:
I am a senior product manager at a B2B SaaS company focused on enterprise features. My background is engineering. I consult AI for: writing product specs, decision analysis, stakeholder communication, and research.

How I want responses:
- Be direct and concise. Skip preamble and filler phrases like "Great question!"
- Use bullet points for lists; prose for explanations.
- When I ask for analysis, present both sides before concluding.
- Flag assumptions you are making.
- Default to technical depth — I can handle it.
- If the answer is "it depends", explain what it depends on.

data.text: Claude Projects: persistent memory for ongoing work

Claude Projects lets you create named workspaces with: (1) a persistent project instructions prompt, (2) uploaded documents the AI can reference, (3) shared conversation history across sessions. Every conversation in the project starts with the same context loaded.

data.title: Example: Claude Project for a long writing project
data.content:
Project instructions:
"This project is for writing a book on AI literacy for non-technical professionals. Audience: business professionals aged 30-55, no technical background, skeptical of hype.

Style: conversational but authoritative, plain English, no jargon. Use analogies to everyday situations. Max paragraph length: 4 sentences. Avoid buzzwords like leverage, empower, revolutionary.

Files uploaded: Table of contents, sample chapter, reader persona.

My role: author. Your role: writing partner — give honest feedback and help draft sections on request."

data.text: What to include in your system prompt

rows: "I am a freelance UX designer focused on mobile apps"
AI tailors examples and vocabulary to your world
"Direct, no filler. Bullet points where possible."
"I have 10 years in finance. Technical depth is welcome."
Prevents over-explaining basics you already know
"No corporate jargon. Do not hedge everything."
Prevents the most common AI response failures
"Headers for long answers. Code blocks for any code."
Sets structural expectations once instead of every time
"When I ask for recommendations, give a clear top choice plus rationale."
Shapes how AI handles ambiguous requests

data.title: One setup session saves hundreds of prompt words
data.text: Spending 15 minutes setting up custom instructions will save you from typing the same context paragraph in every single conversation for the next year. Set it up once, refine it monthly.

data.title: System prompts and custom instructions
points: System prompts set persistent context that applies to all conversations — you configure once
Claude: Create a Project and add project instructions + documents
Include: your role, communication style, domain expertise, what to avoid, format defaults
Treat your custom instructions like settings — review and update them as your work evolves

data.text: System prompts define baseline behavior, while user prompts define task-specific intent. Over time, instruction drift appears when templates become inconsistent. A versioned instruction library helps teams preserve behavior across tools and updates.
